evidence: Receiving P assay: 2.4728 g/L at t=48h (available 52h), below all source comparators (3.057, 3.017, 2.979 g/L at 48h)
Receiving DO2 ~11.8-12.1 mg/L at 50-52h vs sources 10.8-11.5 mg/L — lower uptake consistent with slower production
Receiving P trajectory: 0.034 (12h), 0.0 (24h), 0.885 (36h), 2.473 (48h) — lags source pattern
Physical forward model (nominal, source-calibrated): keep 576.3 kg vs reduce_feed 595.5 kg terminal product mass, min DO 9.2 vs 10.1 mg/L
Sensitivity: reduce_feed feasible in 5/5 members, mass range 590.1-602.0 kg, min DO 9.0-10.9 mg/L
args.rationale: The receiving batch underperforms all three source comparators: latest product assay 2.47 g/L at 48 h vs sources 3.06/3.02/2.98 g/L (~18% lower), and its DO2 runs above source levels at matched times (lower oxygen uptake, slower metabolism). The nominal source-calibrated forward model predicts reduce_feed yields ~595.5 kg terminal product vs ~576.3 kg for KEEP (~+19 kg, ~3%), while remaining feasible with minimum DO ~10 mg/L, far above the 2 mg/L limit. Combined offers no additional product mass over reduce_feed (identical 595.5 kg) and strong_feed_reduction/stop are unwarranted (stop = zero counted production; DO margin already large). The bounded reduce_feed intervention retains full product mass and avoids oxygen-constraint violations.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is a nominal source-calibrated prediction, not truth; hidden receiving parameters (transfer multiplier 1.144, change_h 44h) are estimated, and the ~19 kg gain is model-based. The observed 18% deficit is consistent with, but does not prove, a recoverable metabolic lag; if the lag is due to inoculum state rather than feed balance, gains may be smaller. DO margin is large across all sensitivity members, so oxygen-constraint risk from this action is low either way; the main downside risk is limited (mild feed reduction), making this a low-regret choice.
